newsitem.title: ITALY: Scalfaro calls for Italian unity.
newsitem.headline: Scalfaro calls for Italian unity.

text.p: President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro issued a strong call for Italian unity on Thursday, 10 days ahead of a planned "declaration of independence" for the country's affluent north by the separatist Northern League.

Speaking in Venice, where the League's firebrand leader Umberto Bossi plans to proclaim his northern "republic of Padania" on September 15, Scalfaro urged Italians to look to their "common roots which no one can ever shake".
He spoke of the sacrifice of northern campaigners for Italian unity imprisoned in Venice in the early 19th century, when much of what is now the heartland of Bossi's party was under Austrian rule.
"There were Italians who sacrificed all not for Venice but for Italy. They made no distinction," Scalfaro said at the opening of an art exhibition in the lagoon city.
"They did not think of their own village or their own back yard but of Italy," he said.

Bossi plans to embark on a near-mystical journey along the River Po which dissects Italy and marks the border of his would-be state on Friday next week, starting at its source and culminating in the Venice proclamation.

He has said he expects one million supporters to throng the banks of the Po, forming symbolic human chains along its course, on September 15. Several counter-demonstrations by pro-unity campaigners are planned for the same day.
Bossi has built his party's strength on northern discontent with high taxes and the past corruption and inefficiency of central governments in Rome.

He moved from a federalist to a separatist platform after the League made a strong showing in April's general election, polling almost four million votes in the north, while failing to secure the balance of power in the national parliament.
Recent local elections and an incident last month when Bossi was jeered at an opera in the northern town of Verona suggest his independence drive lacks support even among many League voters.
But he has said he will press ahead and has raised the temperature with a series of inflamatory speeches.
Scalfaro, one of the targets of Bossi's invective, is a northerner himself and one of the founders of Italy's post-war republic.
He told his audience that his last visit earlier this year to Venice followed the destruction of the city's world famous Fenice opera house in a fire.
"Then there were tears for the Fenice and...those tears were the same here as in Sicily, Naples and Rome," he said.
